label: bug
file: src/ingest/parse.ts

The parser only splits input on "\n" (`text.split("\n")`), so it doesn't strip a trailing "\r" from CRLF-terminated lines. The new Windows accounting export tool almost certainly emits CRLF line endings, so the header line ends up as e.g. `["date","amount","description\r"]`. Since "description\r" never matches the required "description" column, `assertShape` fails on the very first line, producing the "Malformed row" error reported at row 1 for every upload. The parser should normalize/strip "\r" (e.g. handle CRLF/CR as well as LF) before splitting fields.
